summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with a history of liver transplant for HCV cirrhosis, chronic kidney disease, and diabetes was admitted for acute kidney injury in the setting of one week of watery diarrhea. Initial evaluation revealed prerenal azotemia likely due to dehydration from diarrhea. She was found to have Clostridium difficile infection, treated with oral vancomycin and metronidazole after initial IV therapy due to symptom recurrence. A concurrent asymptomatic Klebsiella pneumoniae urinary tract infection was treated with ceftriaxone, later switched to oral ciprofloxacin based on sensitivities. Her Myfortic was held during infection to reduce immunosuppression. Transaminases rose during admission, likely due to recurrent hepatitis C, requiring outpatient monitoring. Renal function improved with IV hydration and supportive care, though creatinine remained above baseline. Lower extremity edema persisted, with echocardiogram showing moderate to severe tricuspid regurgitation and pulmonary hypertension, prompting cardiology referral. She was discharged home on antibiotics, with instructions to hold Lasix and Myfortic until further follow-up, and with medication adjustments including metoprolol dosing and anticoagulation prophylaxis.
